thread:
dana: Quick design question: instead of operator returning a rich placement plan, what about a "lease token" model? operator issues short-lived lease tokens with a budget (units) + safety_flags; runtime interprets units to pick model variant and consumption. keeps operator stateless-ish.
leo: Interesting. what's a unit? GPU-second? token credit?
nina: I'd prefer abstract units mapped to billing buckets. runtime translates units -> model_choice via a tenant policy. That lets ops control spend but lets runtime optimize latency.
priya: Important: leases must be single-use or idempotent? we need to avoid double-spend on prewarm credits when runtime retries. also need a clear draining handshake.
kevin: Proto sketch I had in mind:
```
LeaseToken {
  token_id: string
  units: int64        // abstract units (billing buckets)
  expires_at: int64
  safety_flags: [string] // e.g. "no-quant", "min-recall:0.9"
  state: "active" | "draining"
}
```
dana: Safety flags are key. if product sets "no-quant" runtime must never pick a quantized variant. failures should return explicit error and fallback to routing policy.
leo: Who banks units? operator should track allocation but runtime must report consumption with token_id to avoid drift. operator keeps final accounting for billing and SLA.
nina: Operational flow idea: 1) operator mints token and records ledger entry 2) runtime redeems token via an idempotent consume call with token_id and delta_units 3) operator responds with accepted_amount and remaining_units 4) runtime continues.
priya: Edgecases: if operator loses state (leader fail), runtime might have redeemed but operator misses record. need dedupe window (ops should accept idempotent retries for token_id with server-side dedupe).
kevin: Also add a "grace_ttl" field so operator can mark token draining but still honor small inflight consumption for grace_ttl secs. otherwise preempting inflight is messy.
ops-bot: FYI: last week 3 tenants saw "fallback-to-quant" incidents when operator-level cost hints flipped mid-request. Linked investigation: https://incidents/6620000002 :warning:
dana: That incident motivates having explicit immutable safety_flags on the token. if flags change, new tokens required. runtime must reject if token.flags differ from in-memory expectations.
leo: Observability: runtime should emit per-token and per-variant metrics: units_consumed_by_variant, fallback_reason, trace_id for inflight requests that crossed drain boundary. Console needs dashboards for that.
nina: On rollout: start with tokens that have conservative defaults (no safety flags), deploy runtime that treats tokens as advisory unless tenant opts-in to control, then flip enforcement for canary tenants.
priya: We should also standardize a minimal error surface: CLEAR_REJECT (violates safety_flags), INSUFFICIENT_UNITS, TOKEN_EXPIRED, SERVER_ERROR. makes automation simpler.
kevin: One more: allow operator to attach "preferred_model_family" metadata for tenants that want predictable output. runtime should prefer family if units allow it, but can fall back if family unavailable. record audit.
dana: Agree. Next steps: priya to draft lease-token proto + idempotency semantics; kevin to sketch runtime redemption API; nina/leo to draft observability requirements and dashboards. Sync tomorrow 11am?
leo: I'll be there.
priya: sounds good, starting the draft now.
